problem: Camera and actor deviations can leave the logged observation domain before RGB artifacts become obvious, while lateral distance alone cannot express scene-, camera-, actor-, or frontend-dependent support.
mechanism: A parameter-free support certificate combines nearest training-camera position, view angle, and projected observed LiDAR support; lower support should rank RGB/depth/cross-frontend failure within and across equal-distance cohorts.
existing_method_boundary: This is an analytic compiler/verifier baseline, not a new reconstruction or learned support network. If distance explains the result, the learned-support direction is rejected and V6 pivots to provenance/verifier evidence.
failure_ledger_fact: R3 plan requires support to predict downstream failure earlier than pure image quality and not be fully explained by camera distance.
minimum_experiment: Two development scenes, StreetGS and AD-GS, two frames per scene, six lateral offsets, sparse observation RGB/depth support, cross-frontend static/actor/boundary disagreement, plus registered actor edits.
expected_direction: Support invalidity has positive stable rank correlation with downstream error and exceeds absolute lateral distance by at least the frozen margin.
falsification_condition: Support Spearman is below 0.30, gain over distance is below 0.05, distance-residual Spearman is below 0.10, or ordering is not stable across both scenes/frontends.
compute_budget: single RTX 3090; sequential frontend workers; no training; target under 2 GPU-hours and 24,000 MiB peak

problem: A single support scalar cannot distinguish photometric, geometric, semantic and dynamic readiness; R3 already showed that scalar support adds no value over distance and can be falsely safe for frontend-specific geometry failure.
mechanism: Use provenance-aware task-conditioned validity: cross-frontend consistency for q_photo, logged geometry residual plus camera support for q_geometry, actor-boundary evidence plus actor observation denominator for q_semantic, and explicit unknown/abstain for q_dynamics when no independent dynamics verifier exists.
existing_method_boundary: This is a conservative development-benchmark qualification rule over frozen R3 evidence, not a learned confidence model or cross-domain calibration claim.
minimum_experiment: Compare V0 distance, V1 projected view support, V2 logged reconstruction residual, V3 R3 scalar support, and factorized q on all 48 R3 rows; report coverage, selective risk and false-safe per task and per scene.
expected_direction: Factorized validity reduces worst-case false-safe by at least 0.20 versus V3, has nonzero aggregate coverage for photo/geometry/semantic, and abstains on dynamics rather than declaring unsupported cases safe.
falsification_condition: Worst-case false-safe gain over V3 is below 0.20, any accepted factor exceeds 0.05 false-safe, photo/geometry/semantic aggregate coverage is below 0.08, or q_dynamics accepts any case without an independent dynamics verifier.
compute_budget: CPU-only; no training; under 5 minutes; no confirmation read

problem: Before introducing a generator, the compiler must show that an exact held-out oracle proposal can pass independent task checks, survive provenance-preserving bake, and expand the usable region; otherwise the representation, verifier, or bake path is the bottleneck.
mechanism: Create four deterministic observation-plane SceneIR patch pseudo-holes from frozen R3 renders, submit the held-out content as an observed oracle proposal, verify photo/geometry/semantic agreement against the held-out observation, bake accepted proposals only, and reject a matched corrupted decoy control.
existing_method_boundary: This is an oracle upper-bound integration benchmark over development pseudo-holes, not a generation result, dense novel-view ground truth claim, or confirmation calibration result.
minimum_experiment: Two development scenes, StreetGS and AD-GS, two frames, and four pseudo-hole types (missing route support, missing side view, disocclusion, actor removal hole): 32 oracle proposals plus 32 corrupted controls with per-case provenance, verifier decision, bake invariance, and usable-region metrics.
expected_direction: Oracle acceptance is at least 0.95, corrupted-control acceptance is at most 0.05, median masked photo error reduction and eligible depth error reduction are at least 0.90, every hole type gains at least 0.50 usable masked coverage, and pixels outside the bake mask remain byte-identical.
falsification_condition: Oracle acceptance below 0.95, corrupted-control acceptance above 0.05, either median error reduction below 0.90, any hole type usable-coverage gain below 0.50, provenance loss, or any outside-mask mutation.
compute_budget: CPU-only reuse of 80 hash-verified R3 renders; no training; under 10 minutes; no confirmation read
